1. (Currently Amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of __infrared__ light pulses having a first speed; receiving a second sequence of __infrared__ light pulses from a vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of __infrared__ light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of __infrared__ light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, __and wherein the second speed is dynamically determined based on vehicle proximity conditions__.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of __infrared__ light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, __and wherein the computing device adjusts transmission parameters to avoid message collisions__.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of __infrared__ light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed, __and wherein the third speed is selected to optimize communication range__.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of __infrared__ light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of __infrared__ light pulses having a third speed based on the third sequence of __infrared__ light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the third speed is different from the second speed, __and wherein each speed is independently calculated for each vehicle communication__.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the __infrared__ light pulses are modulated IR radiation __transmitted via dedicated infrared transmitters__.

6. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Previously presented) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses.

11. (Currently Amended) An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a __non-transitory__ memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of __infrared__ light pulses having a first speed; receive a second sequence of __infrared__ light pulses from a vehicle; and transmit a message as a sequence of __infrared__ light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of __infrared__ light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, __and wherein the second speed is dynamically determined based on vehicle proximity conditions__.

12. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of __infrared__ light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, __and wherein the computing device adjusts transmission parameters to avoid message collisions__.

13. 14. 15. (Currently Amended) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the __infrared__ light pulses are modulated IR radiation __transmitted via dedicated infrared transmitters__.

16. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

17. (Previously presented) The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.
